hypotheses.reasoning: The login path is edge-proxy → account-svc → auth-svc → identity provider (idp.example). The first sign of trouble is the IdP token call slowing down at 09:53:20 (5.8s, line 2567). From 09:54:12 auth-svc calls to the IdP hang until they hit the 30s timeout (lines 2657, 2746, 2889). account-svc's calls to auth-svc time out on the same traces (t-7441, t-7474, t-7543). The waiting drains account-svc's connection pool to auth-svc: by 09:59:19 checkouts time out (line 3345). As a result, edge-proxy gets 503s from account-svc on POST /login starting at 09:56:20. The IdP hangs instead of failing fast, so this is a dependency timeout, not an external outage.
The IdP is a third-party service, so this could be read as that provider being down. But the logs only show hangs and timeouts, with no 5xx or refused connections.
ingest-api is crashing from running out of memory at the same time, but it sits on the separate /v1/events path. Nothing ties it to the /login failures, so it is a red herring.

verdict.recommendedAction: Check whether the identity provider (idp.example) is healthy and contact the vendor. Lower auth-svc's IdP timeout from 30s and add a circuit breaker or fail-fast so stuck calls don't drain account-svc's pool to auth-svc. If tokens can be cached or validated locally, use that as a fallback. Investigate the ingest-api out-of-memory crashes as a separate issue.
